**Test image observations:**
- Wide field-level view of a soybean field
- Diffuse, widespread yellowing/chlorosis throughout the canopy
- Foreground plants show mixed green and yellow/brown leaves
- Yellowing appears progressive, affecting lower/middle canopy with some leaves turning yellow and dropping
- No distinct circular patches (argues against SCN), no obvious interveinal necrosis pattern (argues against SDS)
- No visible stem lesions, white mold, or wilting collapse

**Reference comparison:**
- **Septoria brown spot** (top-right field view): Very similar diffuse canopy yellowing pattern with scattered yellow leaves among green
- **SCN**: Field view shows yellowing but typically in more circular/lens-shaped patches
- **SDS**: Shows more dramatic interveinal necrosis on individual leaves
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Shows patches of dead plants, more severe
- **Charcoal Rot**: More severe wilting/browning in rows
- **Cercospora/Phytophthora/White Mold**: Clearly different symptom presentations

The progressive, diffuse canopy yellowing with leaves turning yellow and dropping -- starting in the lower/middle canopy -- best matches Septoria brown spot, which causes "leaves to turn yellow and drop" with "defoliation of the lower and middle canopy" and features "small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions" that cause "leaf yellowing [that] expands far beyond the necrotic region."
